Tones are distinctive pitch variations and are contrastive in the language since they can affect the meaning of words/phrases, where the words/phrases consist of exactly the same segmental sequences. ... tone_statements.citation: Brindle, Jonathan (2017). A dictionary and grammatical outline of Chakali. Berlin: Language Science Press. 491 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Chakali is a tone language with both lexical and grammatical tone. Tones are distinctive pitch variations and are contrastive in the language since they can affect the meaning of words/phrases, where the words/phrases consist of exactly the same segmental sequences. [...] Based on the evidence of nominal paradigms, two tones are suggested, i.e. high (H) and low (L). They are transcribed on segments with an acute and a grave accent, respectively. Since tones are assigned to moras, light syllables can get a single tone, i.e. H or L. The heavy syllables may get high (H) or low (L), or either one of the contour tones, i.e. falling (HL) or rising (LH). A mid tone is often perceived, but no contrast is found at the lexical level. Provisionally, the mid tone is said to be a derived tone, that is, a raised low tone or a lowered high tone.

audit.reasoning: The classification 'tonal' (tonal-OR-pitch accent scope exit, no word stress) rests on the only published reference description of Chakali, Brindle 2017 (LangSci, open access), which we hold as publisher PDF + text; the deciding quotation is verbatim at sec. 4.1, pp. 294-295, and a full-text search confirms the phonology outline describes a two-tone (H/L) lexical+grammatical tone system with mora as TBU and never mentions stress or accent as a phonological category. Glottolog's descriptive bibliography and web searches turn up no competing or more specialised prosodic study (no phonology article, JIPA illustration, or instrumental work); the only unheld descriptive item is the author's own unpublished 2011 thesis, which the 2017 book is based on and supersedes. the compilers and the compilers already agreed; this compilation re-confirmed the quote in the copy consulted.
